\chapter{Three Useful Places: Two New Signs}
\label{ch:mw-places-three}
\hlchaptermodality{14}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can recognise, say, read, and write market, home, and temple after learning only \mw{ज} and \mw{घ}.}

Three source-attested destinations begin by ear, add two signs separately, and finish in four scored skills without pretending the location question is taught.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[bājār]{Hear \emph{bājār} — market}

\label{lesson:MW-C10-hear-bajar}



\begin{quote}
Recall the twelve-label payoff and say family once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{bājār} — \textbf{market}
\end{quote}

Hear the two long vowels and say the destination. Its new middle consonant stays off the page until the next lesson.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-5-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 5}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ja]{\mw{ज} — the middle of market}

\label{lesson:MW-W10-ja}



\begin{quote}
Say market and polite yes, write \textbf{\mw{हां}}, \textbf{\mw{बच्चा}}, and familiar \textbf{\mw{च}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one sign}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ज}} — \emph{ja}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace once, copy once, cover the model, and write \textbf{\mw{ज}} from sound.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bājār]{\mw{बाजार} — market on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C10-bajar}



\begin{quote}
Say market and child. Give polite yes, recall the seven-label payoff, then write \textbf{\mw{ब}}, \textbf{\mw{ज}}, \textbf{\mw{ा}}, and \textbf{\mw{र}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{बा}} + \textbf{\mw{जार}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{बाजार}} — \emph{bājār} — market
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write the word. Check both long-vowel marks.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-5-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 5}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ghar]{Hear \emph{ghar} — home}

\label{lesson:MW-C10-hear-ghar}



\begin{quote}
Say and write market, then recall the polite-yes and twelve-label four-skill payoffs.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Say the single beat with breath after the first sound. Writing waits one step.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-5-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 5}.

\section[mandir]{Hear \emph{mandir} — temple}

\label{lesson:MW-C10-hear-mandir}



\begin{quote}
Say home, market, and maternal grandmother, then write \textbf{\mw{ज}} and retroflex \textbf{\mw{ण}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{mandir} — \textbf{temple}
\end{quote}

Say the three short sound groups. The complete spelling uses only earned signs, but meaning stays first.

\section[mandir]{\mw{मंदिर} — a new place from known signs}

\label{lesson:MW-C10-mandir}



\begin{quote}
Say temple, write \textbf{\mw{म}}, \textbf{\mw{ं}}, \textbf{\mw{द}}, \textbf{\mw{ि}}, \textbf{\mw{र}}, \textbf{\mw{ी}}, then write \textbf{\mw{घर}} and \textbf{\mw{नानी}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{मं}} + \textbf{\mw{दि}} + \textbf{\mw{र}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{मंदिर}} — \emph{mandir} — temple
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write the word. Check the nasal mark and the short-i position separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-5-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 5}.
\end{tcolorbox}
